Prevention: Remove crop residues if the problem was seen before.
But do not remove debris and residues if no major pest problem in the field, to improve soil.
In very infested areas, it is important to leave a period of 3 months rotating with grasses (Maize, Sorghum).
Avoiding sequential planting in the infected areas to avoid whitefly spread between fields.
Enhance natural predators of whiteflies (Ladybugs, spiders, lacewing larvae and dragonflies) by planting
Monitoring: Whiteflies suck plant juices and produce a sticky substance (honeydew).
Whiteflies are vectors of viral diseases, such as
Disease which can heavily reduce yield.
When cassava plants are young, scout weekly for whiteflies in the mornings or evenings.
Check undersides of leaves around the veins, even if they aren’t visible, feel leaf surfaces for honeydew.
Look for small whiteflies (0.8-1.0 mm in length), yellow-white coloured body and snow-white tiny wings.
Consider to control when more than 60% of the sampled leaves have at least 10 flies per leaf.4
In case of viruses infections found in nearby fields, you may need to act earlier.
Direct Control: Add 100ml of dish washing liquid and a squeeze of lemon juice into a spray bottle then top up with 5L of water, shake and spray the leaves.
Be sure to spray the undersides of leaves.
Spray at a cooler time of the day.
Use a yellow sticky traps (card or wood with 8x12 cm), then smear with a mixture of petroleum jelly with a little dishwashing liquid.
Hang up close to affected plants to catch and kill adults.
Place 5 traps/500m2 placed 50 cm above the ground.
Spray once a week when thresholds reached.
Restrictions: Chemical insecticides should be avoided, because whiteflies often become quickly resistant
and all you end up doing is killing the beneficial insects.

When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re- entry interval.
